🇹🇭 American tourist choked to death by Italian MMA fighter “Frank the Tank” in Thailand 

A 46-year-old American tourist named Kalif Edward Harper died after being placed in a chokehold by 39-year-old Italian MMA fighter Frank Eric Marques (“Frank the Tank”) at a hotel in Bangkok, Thailand.

Marques, a Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt and former professional MMA fighter, walked past the desk toward the elevator. According to security footage, Harper verbally provoked Marques, who stepped into the elevator and asked, “You talking to me?”

When Harper suggested they “step outside,” Marques retreated into the elevator. CCTV footage shows Harper violently forcing the closing elevator doors open, breaking them, pulling Marques into the lobby, and placing him in a headlock.

Marques overpowered the larger man, pinned him to the floor, and applied a chokehold until Harper’s body went limp. Harper died at the scene.

Marques maintains he acted in self-defense. Despite footage indicating Harper initiated the physical attack, Thai police detained Marques on suspicion of murder, and prosecutors are pursuing a charge of intentional homicide.

posts.text:
Director Mamoru Oshii believes AI has shown that it can't create the kind of meaning and cultural history that comes from human experience

"I think AI is a massive meme-reproduction machine. It's a mechanism for proliferation, isn't it? We're now living in an era where anyone can make anime, anyone can make games, and illustrations can be created in just a few minutes. In this day and age, I find myself wondering what meaning words like "plagiarism" and "fake" even have.

However, you can immediately tell that AI-generated works are different from those created by humans. That's because humans are living beings. We live through our memories. This is something that AI still hasn't been able to overcome, and probably never will. I think AI's greatest achievement has been revealing that this is where human value lies.

That's why animators won't be put out of work, and film directors will still be able to make a living. However, as a tool, AI is already indispensable. I think it will become difficult to work without it.

In a sense, AI has no significance beyond being a resource drawn from the past. No matter how deeply it becomes integrated into society, it cannot create history. Only humans can leave their mark on history. I think AI's greatest achievement has been making that fact clear."
